title: Teach the replay harness which accesses the memory model orders

blocks.text: The platform team's replay harness records every run of a concurrency test as a list of actions, in the order they ran: each thread's reads and writes of fields, its locks and unlocks, its `start()` and `join()` calls. A race report built on the recording has to flag every pair of plain accesses to one field, from two threads, at least one of them a write, that the memory model leaves unordered. Today it is a stub: it can't tell an ordered pair from an unordered one.
`RaceReport.races()` already finds the pairs worth checking. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/RaceReport.java`:

items: `edge(i, j)`: whether a single rule of the memory model orders action `i` before the later action `j`, with no action in between;
`happensBefore(i, j)`: whether the memory model orders action `i` before action `j` at all.

blocks.text: A recorded `JOIN` means the join returned because the other thread had ended. When you're done, the report flags every pair the model leaves unordered and no pair it orders. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests build recordings by hand; nothing in them runs concurrently.

cases.says: two threads that update a counter, each under the same lock, are reported as race-free
a worker given its input before it starts, and joined before its output is read, is reported as race-free
a plain value handed over by a volatile write that the reader reads before using the value is reported as race-free
a plain write that ran before another thread's read, with nothing connecting the two threads, is a race
a write under one lock and a read under a different lock are a race
a volatile write to one field followed by a volatile read of another field connects nothing
a write the starting thread makes after start() is a race with the started thread's read
a write carried to a third thread through a lock handoff and then a start() is ordered, while a later write by the first thread is not

origin.section: An Edge Carries Every Write Made Before It, Only to Code After Its Other End

concepts: Only an unlock and a later lock of the same monitor, a volatile write and a later read of the same field, start() and the started thread, and a thread's end and a join on it connect two threads.
Plain writes made before one edge-forming write are carried by that edge, so the fields handed over need no volatile of their own.
start() orders the writes made before the call, not those the starting thread makes after it.
Happens-before is transitive, so a write reaches a thread that never took part in the first edge of a chain.
